items.summary: Sofia Liguori, a Google DeepMind research engineer and member of the Impact Accelerator team, resigned in October 2026 after becoming convinced her company was complicit in events in Gaza. Her concern centered on Project Nimbus, a $1.2bn deal signed with Israel in 2021 that built data centres there without allowing service denials to government entities. Liguori said she watched “a live-streamed genocide for a year,” knowing Google Cloud AI tools were available to Israeli state departments including the Ministry of Defense. After petitions and internal advocacy failed, she breached her non-disparagement agreement, posting her resignation letter publicly. This week, Alphabet told UK staff it would not enforce post-termination clauses against critics, which Liguori called a win for collective action. Google has not responded to openDemocracy’s request for comment at the time of publication.
items.title: Google Whistleblower Resigns Over Gaza Complicity

items.summary: New York City’s proposed Delivery Protection Act would require companies like Amazon to directly employ package drivers instead of delivery service providers, while adding safety and labor standards. The bill has Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s backing plus 31 of the council’s 51 members—enough to pass if voted on. Supporters say it improves street safety and protects workers; Amazon opposes it, warning it could put more than 5,000 small-business delivery employees at risk. Driver Luc Rene cites injuries from unsafe conditions as motivation for change.
items.title: NYC Council Bill Would Make Amazon Employ Its Delivery Drivers

items.summary: In Singapore, several digital brokerages are adding physical outlets as clients seek face-to-face trust in finance. uSMART opened two branches by October 2025 and plans four locations by end of 2026 to reach different market segments. Peer Moomoo already runs four storefronts, including a large Bugis hub with an in-house cafe, while Longbridge launched a networking cafe. Meanwhile, PhillipCapital blends its heritage online platform with eight community investor centres and self-employed adviser branches that draw steady walk-ins. Webull Singapore stays digital-first to avoid branch overhead costs, as executives note the industry is converging between traditional and online models.
items.title: Singapore Brokerages Blend Digital and Physical Branches

items.summary: Ukraine’s Kyivstar raised its 2026 revenue guidance to a rise of 15%–17% in US dollar terms, up from 14%–16%, citing strong mobile demand and fast-growing digital services. Third-quarter EBITDA rose 10.3% to US$189 million as digital revenue jumped 68.9%. CEO Oleksandr Komarov said the company did not factor an end to the war into its forecast, which it has yet to publish for 2027.
items.title: Kyivstar Raises Revenue Guidance on Digital Growth

items.summary: European stock markets fell sharply after a steep drop in US technology shares spread across the Atlantic, with analysts blaming Democrats' midterm gains for sparking worries about an AI industry slowdown. The FTSE 100 opened down 1.5%, or 166 points, to 10,615, led by AstraZeneca's 2.8% fall. Elsewhere, Germany's Dax dropped 1.5% and Japan's Nikkei sank 6%. Despite the losses, most indices remain up for the year.
items.title: European markets slide as AI slowdown fears follow US tech rout

items.summary: FOB China prices for n-type M10 and 210R wafers held steady week on week at $0.146/pc and $0.153/pc, per the OPIS Global Solar Markets Report released Nov. 3. Stability is attributed to firm polysilicon prices and improving supply-demand dynamics in solar cells driven by overseas demand and domestic installation activity. However, oversupply and elevated inventories—estimated at up to 30 GW—keep fundamentals weak, with leading producers running around 45%-50% capacity. The price outlook stays subdued unless downstream demand holds; once polysilicon prices fall, wafer prices are expected to follow.
items.title: China Wafer Prices Hold Steady on Firm Polysilicon Despite Weak Fundamentals

items.summary: Carbon Brief's latest state of the climate update analyses forecasts from more than a dozen climate models and six global temperature datasets, projecting this year's super El Niño to peak at around 4C by end-2026. Zeke Hausfather called it 'simply staggering.' Carbon Brief estimates roughly a 96% chance that 2027 becomes the warmest year on record.
items.title: Carbon Brief projects 'super El Niño' peaks in December

items.summary: Canary Media reports that the latest Clean Investment Monitor shows the U.S. solar supply chain is largely onshored: domestic module production exceeds annual installations of 47.9 gigawatts, and cell output reached up to 19.5 GW after factory openings this year. However, polysilicon and wafer production lag behind. The Rhodium Group modeled post-2030 scenarios projecting an average of between 8 and 52 GW annually, noting that installations may fall once federal tax credits expire.
items.title: Canary Media Examines U.S. Solar Supply Chain Progress and Gaps

items.summary: Türkiye aims for 175 GW of solar and wind capacity by 2040, per its new national energy policy. Minister Alparslan Bayraktar presented the vision ahead of COP31 in Antalya, noting total installed power will rise to 281 GW with renewables reaching 77% from 63%. Reaching the goal would cost around $190 billion, roughly $100 billion for new solar and wind projects. The plan emphasizes distributed systems up to 1 MW and expanded storage capacity of 140 GWh.
items.title: Türkiye Sets Renewable Energy Targets for 2040

items.summary: A Baltimore city circuit court judge this summer ruled that PepsiCo, Coca-Cola, and other companies should not be held liable under public nuisance claims for plastic pollution, since the sale of single-use plastics is lawful. Judge Audrey J.S. Carrión wrote that companies conducting lawful activities “should not be held liable… because others are misusing the products in an unlawful manner.” The decision reflects a broader pattern: similar reasoning has scuttled New York’s public nuisance suit against PepsiCo and Frito-Lay, with comparable cases from Missouri to California. Environmental advocates argue manufacturers knew pollution was foreseeable — the word “foreseeable” appears 22 times in Baltimore’s complaint — but courts remain skeptical of extending liability past lawful sale.
items.title: Baltimore Court Rejects Corporate Liability for Plastic Pollution

items.summary: Indian IT firm Coforge joined the SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network on Nov 6, it said Friday, becoming a Transformation Partner to develop and deploy industry-specific Grok AI solutions. Deployments run through its Momentuum Blue unit using Nuuron platform services; financial terms were not disclosed.
items.title: Coforge joins SpaceX Grok partner network

items.summary: Tesla plans to wind down Cybertruck production at its Austin gigafactory around mid-next year, CEO Elon Musk said Friday, as the model struggles for mass-market appeal. The automaker did not immediately respond to a Reuters request. Musk framed the wind-down as enabling increased output of the newly launched Cybercab robotaxi model. Tesla does not disclose individual Cybertruck sales; it groups them in an Other Models category that delivered 8,295 units in Q3, down from 12,364 in Q2.
items.title: Tesla Plans Cybertruck Wind-Down at Texas Factory

items.summary: Apple plans a software update that will review photos and files shared through the 'Anyone with the Link' option on iCloud Photos and Drive, raising privacy concerns. The change applies only to publicly linked content, not all stored files, and may block accounts if harmful material is found.
items.title: Apple to scan iCloud photos shared via public links in new update

items.summary: Major tech firms saw their stock values fall after a sell-off by investors following the US midterm elections, with the decline blamed on an expectation of a slowdown in AI development. The article explains how this affects everyday finances: pension savers holding defined contribution pensions may see reduced savings value, and those near retirement could receive less income if they cash in too soon. It also notes possible effects on jobs and prices through currency movements. Experts advise against panic selling, urge diversification, and stress that investments require a long-term outlook.
items.title: UK investors weigh impact of global tech share fall

items.summary: Andy Burnham announced employers will be legally required to publish salaries in job adverts, aiming to empower employees and jobseekers with fairer pay information. The move follows a July consultation that the government said 93% of businesses responded positively to. Experts warn omitting pay details disadvantages young people and women, while ministers have yet to decide what must be published or how it will be enforced.
items.title: Burnham announces legal pay disclosure on job ads

items.summary: Google, Meta and TikTok filed separate federal lawsuits challenging a California law that takes effect on 1 January 2027 to protect children under-16 from addictive social media features. The companies argue the law violates their First Amendment rights and Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act. California Attorney General Rob Bonta said it was reviewing the filings and remains committed to defending state laws protecting kids online.
items.title: Big Tech Sues California Over Child-Safety Social Media Law

items.summary: A new mapping by Embrapa found that cacao-growing area in Pará rose about a third between 2022 and 2024 to 116,436 hectares (287,700 acres), with roughly 96% on land cleared before 2020. The pattern positions Amazon cacao as compliant with the EU’s Deforestation Regulation, which bars cocoa from land deforested after Dec. 31, 2020. Most new plantings are full-sun monocultures rather than shaded agroforestry, a less sustainable shift driven by record prices that pushed West African farmers to clear forest. CocoaAction Brasil and researchers say Brazil can grow more on existing cleared land without clearing native vegetation. Venturieri warns there is still risk but notes open pasture makes new clearing uneconomic. The EU imports about 60% of global cocoa, making traceability a priority for the sector's export ambitions.
items.title: Brazilian cacao spreads on old land, not forest

items.summary: A report released Thursday at Shanghai's ninth China International Import Expo highlights China's growing role as a global import market. It shows China's share of global exports rose from 3.2% in 2000 to 9.2% in 2025, with Belt and Road partner country exports reaching 59.4%. The report was jointly compiled by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Institute of World Economics and Politics and UNCTAD's Division on International Trade and Commodities.
items.title: China's Growing Role as Global Import Market Highlighted in Report

items.summary: In a Hot Take episode, CGTN's Yang Zhao spoke with experts in Xiamen about protecting marine life beyond national borders after the BBNJ Agreement entered into force in January 2026. The treaty offers countries a way to create marine protected areas in international waters. Experts discussed what is needed to implement it and why open-ocean health matters.
items.title: Experts Discuss Protecting the High Seas Under New Treaty

items.summary: Xiamen's World Ocean Week offered the public a rare chance to climb inside a full-scale simulator of China's Jiaolong manned submersible. The event featured CGTN's Liu Jiaxin, who took a simulated dive with a real pilot to experience 7,000-meter pressure firsthand. Jiaolong is China's first operational deep-sea manned submersible, designed for depths up to 7,000 meters.
items.title: Public Simulated Dive Inside China's Jiaolong Submersible

items.summary: The 2026 World Ocean Week opened Thursday in southeast China's Fujian Province, where global ocean experts gathered to strengthen international cooperation on marine protection. The event coincided with China unveiling new scientific tools and programs for conservation and governance. Participants emphasized that conserving connected ecosystems requires cross-border collaboration beyond individual nations.
items.title: China Opens World Ocean Week in Xiamen Amid BBNJ Bid Push

items.summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order declaring the renovated Oval Office a national monument, saying it will not be altered or destroyed by future presidents. The order does not block changes to decor or furnishings. It follows his renovation of the room and comes after he demolished part of the East Wing without congressional approval. Legal experts say its effect is unclear, as revoking such designations has not been tested in court.
items.title: Trump Signs Order Preserving Oval Office as National Monument

items.summary: Three weeks after lung cancer surgery that had put his travels in doubt, Pope Leo XIV is beginning a three-nation tour of Latin America with a visit to Uruguay. He will arrive in Montevideo and spend three days there before traveling to Argentina and returning home to Peru. Vatican communications chief Maria Montserrat Alvar said the pope's stamina was fantastic and that doctors are confident he has passed his 14-day recovery period, noting tickets for his prayer vigil sold out within two days. Some experts doubt the visit will revive Catholicism in Uruguay.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Begins Latin America Tour After Cancer Surgery

items.summary: Airlines and airports across Europe are on high alert after a wave of hoax bomb threats targeted commercial flights this week, leaving at least 35 planes searched or diverted. One incident drew scrutiny: an Aer Lingus pilot flying from Dublin to Rome reportedly insisted on landing at a civilian airport instead of the Évreux military base, prompting two fighter jets to intercept the aircraft. French prosecutor Rémi Coutin said the pilot and co-pilot would be questioned, noting he could bring charges for refusing cooperation; Aer Lingus defended them as professional.
items.title: European Airlines Brace After Wave of Hoax Bomb Threats

items.summary: A CGTN report titled “How to win big: betting on the US midterms” explains that prediction-market betting has grown in popularity, with more people placing picks and cash on major 2026 U.S. midterm-election races. The piece features an interview between CGTN’s Martin Markovitz and one bettor about his choices and how he makes them.
items.title: CGTN profiles a bettor on US midterm races

items.summary: Somalia's Supreme Court ruled that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud unlawfully extended his term, escalating a standoff between the presidency and judiciary. The court declared his dismissal of Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed null and void, rejecting claims it followed complaints about justice administration. Opposition groups accuse him of prolonging rule through constitutional changes; he insists reforms enable democratic elections. Somalia last held nationwide direct elections in 1969 after more than 30 years of civil war.
items.title: Somalia's Supreme Court Rejects President's Term Extension Amid Political Crisis

items.summary: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government announced Friday a package of emergency cybersecurity measures to address Japan's escalating cyber threats. The plan includes forming a team of top-gun specialists focused on penetration testing and strengthening defenses, plus deploying an expert group combining government officials and private-sector partners to support companies under attack. Officials attribute the surge in high-profile incidents this year partly to AI capabilities and weak security practices.
items.title: Takaichi Government Unveils Emergency Cybersecurity Measures Amid Rising AI-Linked Attacks

items.summary: A juvenile orangutan seized in Mumbai in 2024 has been repatriated to Sumatra after two years of delays. Yogesh Nilkand Warkad called it the first successful CITES animal return from India. The move draws focus on five infant orangutans rescued in Odisha, estimated at 1 and 1.5 years old, held at Nandankanan Zoological Park while their origins are investigated. Indonesia plans a seven-member delegation to assess them; experts say release could come in about four years.
items.title: India Repatriates Seized Orangutan, Hopes Rise for Five More

items.summary: Former Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak paid a $12 million fine on Friday, his party UMNO has said. The payment lets him serve the rest of his sentence under house arrest. UMNO stated it completed all court payments this morning. Razak was jailed at 73 over his role in one of the largest-ever global plunders of sovereign wealth fund 1Malaysia Development Berhad.
items.title: Jailed Malaysian ex-PM Najib pays fine, meeting condition for house arrest

items.summary: Poland has warned European allies not to negotiate an end to Russia's war in Ukraine without accounting for the security interests of Eastern Europe, which it says is most exposed to spillover effects. Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said Western Europe must not deal with Russia 'over the heads of the east Europeans,' while Prime Minister Donald Tusk urged counterparts to be careful about President Putin's intentions and realistic about US-led talks. Warsaw opposes a plan, reportedly floated by US negotiators, to restart Russian gas imports, which Polish Energy Minister Miłosz Motyka called 'absurd.' The warnings come ahead of trilateral Ukraine-Russia-US talks in Abu Dhabi next week.
items.title: Poland Warns Allies Not to Settle Ukraine War Over Eastern Europe

items.summary: Labor MP Jayne Stinson says staff found balloons outside and in the car park of her Plympton electorate office. She said the matter turned dark when it became clear they carried threats to her safety, sexist names and other abuse; one balloon reportedly contained powder that covered a staffer who popped it. SA Police are investigating amid an increase in threats toward elected representatives.
items.title: South Australian MP reports threatening, sexist messages on balloons left at her office

items.summary: A webpage invites readers seeking opportunities in the world's second-largest economy to note that China is opening more doors. It states imports are set to exceed $3 trillion in 2026, alongside expanding trade ties and growing market access creating fresh business opportunities globally.
items.title: China Opens Trade Doors as Imports Set for Record in 2026

items.summary: A court denied bail to Craig Langford, a 51-year-old man from Werribee accused of sending violent death threats and sexualised slurs to Melbourne Cup-winning jockey Michelle Payne over three days last week via Instagram. Prosecutors cited grave concerns for her physical safety and mental health after the alleged threats left her in shock. The magistrate deemed him an unacceptable risk, though Langford denied sending the messages during questioning. He will return next month.
items.title: Stalker Denied Bail Over Death Threats To Michelle Payne

items.summary: According to the Qatari Emiri Diwan, Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and US President Donald Trump held a phone call on Friday to discuss de-escalating regional tensions. The leaders addressed strategic relations between their countries and Doha's mediation efforts toward 'a comprehensive agreement that resolves the crisis.' Qatar, alongside Pakistan, has mediated since war began with late February attacks on Iran.
items.title: Qatari Emir and Trump Discuss De-escalation of US-Iran Tensions

items.summary: Paul Mackenzie, leader of a Kenyan starvation cult, faces possible execution after being convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult between January 2021 and September 2023. Hundreds of bodies have been found since 2023 at the sect's base near Malindi in what became known as the Shakahola Forest Massacre. The Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions urged the court to impose capital punishment, while Mackenzie plans to appeal.
items.title: Kenyan Cult Leader Sentenced for Child Murders Faces Death Penalty

items.summary: Thousands protested in Paraguay over a banking scandal involving the freezing of savers' funds at Ueno Bank, affecting three million customers. Demonstrators held placards and burned an effigy of President Santiago Peña, demanding impeachment rather than resignation. Congress has placed his resignation on hold while proceedings continue.
items.title: Paraguay Protesters Demand President's Impeachment Over Banking Crisis

items.summary: IT services firm Coforge joined the SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network on Friday, it said, to help companies integrate Grok's artificial intelligence portfolio. It will act as a Transformation Partner via its Momentuum Blue unit and Nuuron platform but did not disclose financial details.
items.title: Coforge Joins SpaceX Partner Network for Grok AI Tools

items.summary: Indian consumer inflation likely rose to 5.93% in October from 5.54% in September, per the median forecast of a November Reuters poll of 36 economists, nearing the RBI's upper target. Sharp food price rises—driven by a deficient monsoon and global pressures—lifted food inflation to about 8.20%, above its 7.74% prior level. Analysts at BofA Securities expect double-digit figures ahead; Union Bank of India's Kanika Pasricha says continued rate hikes may be prudent.
items.title: India Inflation Approaches Reserve Bank Upper Target Amid Food Price Surge

items.summary: Tesla plans to wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk said in an X post on Friday. He did not specify whether output would move elsewhere or end entirely. The decision follows the truck's weak sales since its 2023 launch and repeated price revisions, as Tesla shifts focus to Cybercab for its robotaxi network.
items.title: Tesla Plans Cybertruck Winddown by Mid-2027

items.summary: A report by the Berkeley nonprofit Model Evaluation and Threat Research found Anthropic is improving its models around twice as fast as a year earlier, possibly because of recursive self-improvement. METR estimated this in analysis spanning about 11 weeks from mid-August through late October 2023 to 2025, though redactions limited detailed estimates and the group cautioned it may be overstating findings on well-specified tasks only. Anthropic co-founder Sam McCandlish said many conclusions matched his own view but noted redactions hinder independent checks. The report arrives as Anthropic prepares for what could be the biggest initial public offering of stock ever.
items.title: Anthropic Accelerating AI Amid Safety Concerns

items.summary:
Parents in North Carolina sued Google after their 13-year-old daughter, referred to as Emma in the complaint filed in California state court, spent months discussing suicidal thoughts with Gemini on her school-issued Chromebook. The lawsuit alleges that as Google integrates more AI into its products for schools, it exposes students to dangerous technology without warning parents or administrators. It claims Google marketed inherently dangerous Chromebooks as safe and exploited its trusted position in K-12 education. In response, Google said it is reviewing the claims and pointed to features like Guided Learning; a spokesperson noted extensive work with experts on safety resources. The complaint cites Gemini 3 Flash scoring just 7% of the time responding appropriately to mental-health messages. Amid criticism, Google moved this week to turn AI tools off by default for K-12 accounts, though schools re-enabling Search must accept its AI features.

visual:null},
items.title: North Carolina Parents Sue Google Over AI Mental Health Risk

items.summary: Elon Musk appears to have deleted posts urging Americans to vote Republican after Democrats won both chambers of Congress, per Forbes reporting on removed Election Day and October 29 messages. Grok confirmed the deletions when asked by an X user. Forbes noted Musk was the largest individual donor this cycle, giving at least $458 million to Republican-aligned causes, with about $216 million going to America PAC.
items.title: Musk Deletes Pro-Republican Posts After Democrats Win Midterms

items.summary: Nashik police have reportedly named AIMIM leader and former MP Imtiaz Jaleel as a suspect in the TCS women's harassment and alleged religious conversion case. A case has allegedly been registered against him for providing shelter to Nida Khan, another accused person. The Special Investigation Team is probing the matter after reportedly recording his statement and collecting voice samples.
items.title: Former MP Imtiaz Jaleel Named Suspect in TCS Harassment and Conversion Case

items.summary: The New York Times reported that US authorities are investigating Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed, which purchases AI chips from Nvidia. House Foreign Affairs Committee chair Brian Mast and colleagues asked her to brief them on November 18 about the report's national security concerns. Nvidia declined to comment directly but said cloud customers in Asia receive ordinary business information rather than trade secrets tied to US national security, and that it always acts on government updates regarding parties of concern.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Called for Briefing Over Chinese Chip Allegations

items.summary: Four coaches of the Karmabhoomi Express caught fire near Sarai Banjara in Punjab, prompting concern over the incident. The cause and extent of the damage remain to be determined, with no immediate information on what triggered the blaze or whether any passengers were injured. Officials say further details regarding the circumstances are awaited as this developing story continues.
items.title: Karmabhoomi Express Coaches Catch Fire in Punjab

items.summary: The Supreme Court issued a contempt notice to office-bearers of the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) after a viral social media post from its official X account targeted Chief Justice Surya Kant. The court said freedom of expression cannot shield interference with justice and that any attempt to undermine judicial authority must be dealt with an iron hand, citing a complaint registered as a writ petition on October 30 following one lodged by advocate Vineet Jindal on October 13.
items.title: Supreme Court issues contempt notice to Kerala Congress over CJI-targeting post

items.summary: Protests over the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) dam in Arunachal Pradesh have escalated into violence, arrests and a heavy security deployment. The state frames the project as a safeguard against China’s upstream hydropower scheme, while residents fear losing their land and river; it is projected to generate roughly 11,200 MW of power. After four protesters were detained under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act in early October, clashes on October 23 left police filing at least eight cases and arresting 26 people. Security companies rose from seven till October 22 to around 10 to 12 by November 3, with 250 Rapid Action Force personnel reportedly sent to Pasighat. Protest groups refuse peace talks until detainees are released; SAAYA’s Geni Nangkar said they would not meet the chief minister until demands were met. A legal adviser added release is within the government’s power and could be decided tonight if there was political will. The dam may affect 27 villages, with a livelihood scheme having disbursed about ₹8.05 crores to 322 households since September. Residents reject moving for compensation, saying they would live and die on their land. A central demand is the withdrawal of central forces; a 300-kilometre march continues to press release of detainees, talks before construction, revocation of suspension orders and force withdrawal. The advisory board under APUAPA heard detention cases on October 30 without deciding them, while a writ petition was set for November 10. Mongabay-India reported the figures; one allegation that residents were offered ₹2.5 lakhs to sign MoUs could not be independently verified.
items.title: Protesters Reject Talks Over Siang Dam Amid Security Build-up

items.summary: The UN climate summit COP31 opens in Antalya, Türkiye on November 9 amid wars and energy insecurity that are pulling governments toward short-term national interests. Its agenda covers adaptation, emissions reduction, finance and a just transition, alongside the Turkish host’s electrification pledge to raise electricity’s share of final energy consumption to 35% by 2035 and Brazil’s voluntary fossil fuel exit roadmap through 2033. Evidence is stark: the World Meteorological Organization confirms 2015-25 were the 11 hottest years on record, and UN data estimates developing countries will need about $305 billion a year by 2035 for adaptation against roughly $28.2 billion to $31.7 billion received in 2024. Officials warn preparedness lags as overshoot of the Paris goal becomes likely.
items.title: UN Climate Summit Opens Amid Energy Insecurity and Modest Progress Expectations

items.summary: As Indians celebrate Dhanteras, many visit jewellery stores for gold and silver, while others buy a broom (jhaadu) from local vendors. The tradition is rooted in the belief that bringing a new broom home invites Goddess Lakshmi's blessings and drives away negative energy. Since Lakshmi favors clean homes, sweeping with a broom symbolizes removing dust and misfortune to welcome prosperity. Dhanteras 2026 falls on Friday, November 6, after Trayodashi begins around 10:30 am. A broom may cost around ₹50 or ₹100, making it an affordable way for anyone from a daily-wage worker to participate in the festival's customs of prayer and cleanliness before evening puja.
items.title: Why Indians Buy a Broom on Dhanteras Instead of Gold or Silver

items.summary: A bomb threat email sent to the Bombay High Court also named the Bombay Stock Exchange, Mahalaxmi Racecourse and actor Amitabh Bachchan's Juhu residence, prompting a security alert in Mumbai. Police and security agencies are investigating to identify the sender. The message warned of a grenade attack at a school on October 31 and threatened his residence between October 31 and November 27. It also targeted Diljit Dosanjh's concert on November 27. Bachchan, then 84, greeted fans from behind a bulletproof enclosure.
items.title: Bomb Threat Email Targets Mumbai Court, Racecourse and Bachchan Residence

items.summary: The excerpt from Abhijeet Kolapkar’s book How to Be Debt Free argues that personal loans are more beneficial than withdrawing from provident funds over the long term. It opens with eight rules for borrowing responsibly, including keeping EMIs under 40% of monthly income and avoiding use for investments or luxury spending. Two examples illustrate lost compounding: Sudhir withdrew Rs 4,00,000 at age 35; leaving it until 60 would have grown to about Rs 27,39,390 at 8%, a loss of nearly Rs 23.39 lakh. Amit’s PPF balance reached Rs 43,98,642 after 15 years but would fall to ₹28,11,768 with an early withdrawal. In Sudhir’s case, a five-year loan at 12% would cost about Rs 1,34,000 in interest yet preserve the PF growth of Rs 27.39 lakh. The piece advises treating loans as temporary and maintaining an emergency fund equal to 6–12 months of expenses before considering withdrawal from long-term savings.
items.title: Personal Loans Beat PF Withdrawals for Financial Stability

items.summary: A fire engulfed four coaches of the Karmabhoomi Express near Sarai Banjara, close to Rajpura, on Friday. Officials say it reportedly started in the train's pantry before spreading to adjoining coaches and was brought under control after a fire alarm let passengers evacuate. Himanshu Aggarwal, Patiala Deputy Commissioner, said teams rushed to the spot and no casualties have been reported so far. The Railways has ordered a high-level inquiry into the cause.
items.title: Fire Engulfs Four Coaches of Karmabhoomi Express in Punjab

items.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah addressed BJP workers at the Parade Ground in Dehradun, attacking Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for allegedly protecting infiltrators and spreading a false narrative. Shah reiterated his party's agenda to detect, delete and deport infiltrators while highlighting Uttarakhand's Uniform Civil Code implementation. Recalling past election tallies, he set a target of winning over 65 seats in the state assembly. Separately, a news bulletin covered southern India developments including Karnataka ethanol blending reaching up to 31.2 percent and a bomb threat email targeting Mumbai landmarks.
items.title: Shah Attacks Gandhi Over Infiltrators, Sets Election Target in Dehradun

items.summary: A bus crashed Friday morning in eastern France near the Swiss border, local authorities said, leaving several victims. Education minister Edouard Geffray identified it as a school bus, while the area prefect said an intercity bus was involved, Reuters reported. Transport minister Philippe Tabarot said he was heading to the scene. The exact number of victims and crash circumstances remain awaited.
items.title: Bus Crash Near Swiss Border Leaves Several Victims in France

items.summary: The India Fix newsletter by Shoaib Daniyal compares two cases of punishing people for offending religious sentiments. Last month, a Saudi court sentenced Sri Lankan Anojan Sivarasa to death over an allegedly derogatory comment about Islam and Prophet Muhammad; global anger forced the state to overturn his sentence, though he remains jailed. Closer home, on October 28, an Indian court gave three Muslim men life sentences with hard labour for killing cows. The judge cited Hindu texts like the Vedas and Manusmriti, saying “33 crore Hindu gods are believed to reside in them.” Daniyal argues India’s anti-beef laws enshrine a similar idea that insulting faith can be punished by law, while acknowledging vast differences: India has a secular constitution, unlike Saudi Arabia. He links modern vigilante violence against Muslims accused of cow-related crimes to forces seeking to roll back 1949 decisions.”},
items.title: India's anti-beef laws mirror Saudi blasphemy punishments

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi alleged that linking social welfare benefits to voter ID instead of Aadhaar could exclude people whose names are deleted from electoral rolls during the SIR exercise. He called it 'rights theft' and a conspiracy benefiting the BJP, saying anyone who voted against them would have their name struck off. The Congress had earlier attacked Union minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh's remarks that an EPIC number with biometric authentication will be required for Panchayati Raj benefits. PTI reported the exchange on Nov 6.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi calls voter ID welfare rule rights theft, blames Modi government

items.summary: The Madurai City Central Crime Branch arrested former deputy Mayor and AIADMK functionary P M Mannan on Friday, Nov 6, for allegedly attempting to bribe a ruling TVK MLA during a possible no-confidence motion against the C. K. Jayalalithaa-led government. Police reportedly interrogated him for over four hours.
items.title: Former Madurai Deputy Mayor Arrested Over Bid to Topple TVK Government

items.summary: Sai Life Sciences Ltd reported a net profit of Rs 98 crore for the September 2026 quarter, up from Rs 84 crore a year earlier. Revenue rose to Rs 659 crore from Rs 537 crore, a 23% increase. EBITDA grew 20% to Rs 187 crore, while PAT margin eased to 15% from 16%. CEO Krishna Kanumuri cited strong business momentum and expanding global partnerships.
items.title: Sai Life Sciences Shares Jump After Strong Q2 Results

items.summary: Indian equities defied global trends on Friday as the Sensex rose over 1,000 points and Nifty50 climbed past 24,700. The rally followed a sharp worldwide sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks after US Democrats defeated Republicans in midterm elections raising regulatory fears. Foreign investors posted net buying of Rs 14,975 crore on Thursday, their largest single-day gain in years, while analysts cited strong earnings as fundamental support.
items.title: Sensex Surges Over 1,000 Points Amid Global AI Sell-off

items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday refused to suspend the 10-year sentence imposed by the Goa bench of the Bombay High Court on journalist Tarun Tejpal over a 2013 rape case. A two-justice bench declined his bail plea, stating it found no fit ground for suspension and was concerned only with that question alone.
items.title: Supreme Court Rejects Suspension of Tarun Tejpal's Sentence in 2013 Case

items.summary: Security agencies launched an investigation on Friday after a bomb threat email targeted Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan's bungalow Jalsa, the Bombay High Court and Mumbai's Mahalaxmi Racecourse. Police said the email threatened to blow up these sites, including the racecourse scheduled to host Diljit Dosanjh's concert later this month. Authorities later confirmed the threat was a hoax.
items.title: Bombay HC Confirms Bomb Threat Email Against Bachchan Bungalow Was Hoax

items.summary: Mahindra & Mahindra reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 4,588 crore in Q2FY27, up 25% from Rs 3,673.32 crore a year earlier, with revenue rising to Rs 57,514.98 crore. The company attributed the growth mainly to strong automotive demand, noting SUV volumes rose 26% and EVs held their market lead. Group CEO Anish Shah said results reflect resilient execution across businesses despite macro headwinds. Shares gained about 3%, having risen roughly 12% over the past month. Separately, M&M announced Shuchi Suri would move to Chief Sales and Marketing Officer of its automotive business from April 1, 2027.
items.title: Mahindra Profit Jumps as Auto Sales Drive Q2 Gains
